correctness.rationale: The individual vertex offspring count has the Poisson-binomial law Σ_j Ber(q_j). Product lower bound Π_{j≤k}q_j gives the log-tail lower estimate, while the generating-product/Chernoff split at k and 2k gives matching exponents −c k^(β+1)/(β+1) or −s k log k. A union bound over n candidates gives a dyadic-summable upper error. Roughly n/(k+1) separated k-child forcing events depend on disjoint Z_t samples and give exp(−n^δ) lower error. Both maxima are monotone; dyadic interpolation gives full a.s. limits. Check k growing sublinearly, s>1, full support, positive vertices only. Finite checker logs are not relied upon as an infinite proof.
